title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
abstract: arXiv:2610.20288v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. translated_title: 预测未见过的科学交互作用：条件流模型会幻觉出非加性效应
translated_abstract: 条件生成模型越来越多地被用于超出直接训练支持范围的科学预测。然而，科学问题往往关注的是一种干预是否会改变另一种干预的效果。这类交互作用可能是核心研究目标，却在总变异中仅占很小比例，这使得模型可能在整体上表现准确，却未能恢复出相关的科学效应。目前尚不清楚这些模型如何学习交互作用，以及它们何时能够成功外推到未见过的条件。因此，我们利用生理时间序列模拟器、药物剂量-反应数据、组合细胞扰动以及分子构象生成，研究流匹配模型中的交互作用恢复问题，并将真实的交互作用恢复与幻觉出的交互结构区分开来。在受控环境中，个体效应的学习远早于交互作用，且模型会在不存在交互作用的地方幻觉出交互结构。在各种设置中，我们……
tldr: 本研究揭示条件流匹配模型学习个体效应远早于学习交互作用，并会在不存在交互作用时幻觉出非加性效应，导致模型整体看似准确却无法恢复真正的科学交互效应。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that conditional flow-matching models learn individual effects much earlier than interactions and hallucinate non-additive effects where none exist, allowing models to appear accurate overall while failing to recover the true scientific interaction effects.
